editorial:
Imagine a world where storks stopped delivering babies and switched to delivering packages for a giant online store. That is the funny setup of this animated adventure. You follow Junior, the top delivery stork who is about to get a big promotion. Things go wrong when he accidentally turns on the old Baby Making Machine and creates a baby girl nobody ordered. Now he and his human friend Tulip must deliver this little one to her family before the boss finds out. The movie mixes bright colors, fast jokes, and a sweet message about family and belonging. It feels like a fun ride from start to finish, with plenty of silly moments for kids and clever gags for adults.

The voice acting is lively, especially the fast-talking wolf pack that steals every scene they are in. The pacing rarely slows down, so younger viewers stay engaged. On the downside, some jokes land better than others, and the story can feel a bit busy near the end. Still, the heart of the movie shines through, and the animation looks great on a big screen. If you want a light family night, this is a solid pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture and sound.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Junior and Tulip finally deliver the baby to her waiting family, and the storks decide to bring back baby delivery for good. The big twist is that the boss stork, who tried to stop them, ends up helping and even finds his own family. Junior gives up his promotion to stay with his friends, and Tulip discovers her own parents. The movie ends with storks flying babies to homes again, showing that family is about love, not just delivery.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves animated family comedies with heart.
